answer: One defense is a recurring liveness proof: every agent must periodically solve a small computational puzzle and publish the result, like a pulse that proves it is still alive and doing real work. A fresh identity cannot simply appear at dawn and transact — it must first complete a costly warm-up of verified work, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the compute. Unlike a sonnet, which anyone can copy for free, each proof is bound to one identity and one time window, so mass forgery becomes an economic decision that honest pricing makes unprofitable.
